title: Sell Mineral Rights in Crane, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Crane, MT
metaDescription: Crane sits in Richland County near the Elm Coulee Field, Montana's original Bakken discovery ground. A former engineer explains what that means for your offer.
heroLead: Crane sits close enough to Elm Coulee that I treat it as genuinely core Bakken MT territory, not the flank language I use for most of this state.
intro: Richland County is where Montana's Bakken story actually started. The Elm Coulee Field, discovered in 2000 near Sidney, became the play's first proof that horizontal drilling in the Bakken and Three Forks could work economically, years before the North Dakota boom took off in earnest. Crane sits within reach of that field, which puts it in a different conversation than most of the towns on this list.

sections.heading: Why Elm Coulee Still Matters
paragraphs: Elm Coulee has been producing for over two decades now, which means wells in and around Crane are further along their decline curves than a freshly drilled North Dakota unit, but it also means there's real, long production history to evaluate. If you're already receiving royalty from an Elm Coulee-area well, that check has likely declined from its early peak, which is normal shale-well behavior, not a sign anything's wrong.

sections.heading: Checking Your Unit's Current Status
paragraphs: A tract in this part of Richland County may sit in a pooled unit that's seen additional wells drilled over the years, or it may still be a single-well unit from the field's earlier development. Either way, comparing your current division order against your original lease is worth doing, since net revenue interest changes as units get reconfigured.

sections.heading: What Drives Value Near Crane
paragraphs: I look at production decline on your specific well or unit, whether the operator has drilled any newer wells nearby, and how your recorded interest compares to current payments. Given the county's history, this is one of the stronger areas in the Bakken MT footprint for both producing and undeveloped interests, and I'll give you a straight number range based on the actual data rather than a generic flank-county estimate.

faqs.question: Is Crane, MT part of the Elm Coulee Field?
faqs.answer: Crane sits in Richland County within reach of the Elm Coulee Field, Montana's original Bakken discovery area from 2000. Whether your specific tract falls inside an Elm Coulee unit depends on the exact parcel, which a title check will confirm.

faqs.question: Why has my royalty check declined over the years near Crane?
faqs.answer: Shale wells like those in Elm Coulee produce most heavily in their first year or two, then decline steadily. A lower check today than five years ago is normal well behavior, not necessarily a problem with your interest.

faqs.question: Where do I check title on Richland County minerals?
faqs.answer: The Richland County Clerk and Recorder in Sidney holds the recorded deeds, leases, and division orders for tracts in and around Crane.
